result.rationale: The handler does `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` but then filters with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` against the raw, non-lowercased guest string, so a differently-cased email bypasses the blacklist. Likewise `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and the isAttendee check compare case-sensitively, allowing duplicate attendee additions under different casing. Emails are not normalized anywhere in the schema (`z.string().email()`) or handler.

judged_text: Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat the blacklist and dedup: blacklist entries are lowercased but compared against the raw guest string (so `BLOCKED@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`), and the `guest === attendee.email` and `isAttendee` checks are case-sensitive, allowing the same person to be added twice under different casing; emails should be normalized (trim/lowercase) at the schema boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase, but the comparison uses the raw `guest` string (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so different casing can bypass the blacklist. Likewise, dedup/identity checks are case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email` in the `uniqueGuests` filter, and `attendee.email === user.email` for `isAttendee`), allowing the same email to be treated as distinct when casing differs. The schema (`z.string().email()`) does not normalize casing/whitespace, so normalization at the boundary is not enforced.
